prediction.beta: New mode in testing — predict BTC's 5-minute direction. Prices, settlement rule and taker fees follow polymarket.com.
prediction.title: BTC 5-minute prediction
prediction.targetTip: Chainlink 60-second time-weighted average price (TWAP) at the moment the round opened; this is Polymarket's price to beat. Settlement uses the 60-second TWAP at the close: at or above it is Up, below is Down.
prediction.upTip: Probability price: 50¢ = the market gives a 50% chance of going up. Higher price, stronger conviction.
prediction.downTip: Probability price: 50¢ = the market gives a 50% chance of going down. Higher price, stronger conviction.
prediction.estPayoutTip: Right prediction: every contract settles at $1. Payout = amount ÷ probability price; the fee is charged on top of the amount.
prediction.feeTip: Polymarket taker fee: shares × 7% × price × (1 − price). Most expensive at 50¢ (1.75¢ per share), cheaper toward the extremes.
prediction.estProceedsTip: What you receive at the current sell price, after fees.
prediction.mySharesTip: Contracts you hold; each is worth $1 if the prediction is right.

jev.title: Jev predictor
jev.intro: Jev bets on BTC's 5-minute up/down market. Three arms now run side by side on the same market, each with its own account and run number and its own books: v5-1 buys on every jump, v5-2 lets Jev check the jump first, and v5-3 lets Jev's read decide buys and sells on the clock. Switch runs above; runs with an arm name after the number are these three, the rest are archives of earlier versions.

armIntro.JUMP_CODE: Arm v5-1 of the three: buy on every jump, without Jev. From 30 to 270 seconds after the open, when UP or DOWN rises {{jump}}¢ or more within 3 seconds from a starting price of {{from}}¢–{{to}}¢, it buys the side that rose; at most one buy per window, held to the close. Jev still answers the questions, for the record only.
armIntro.JUMP_JEV: Arm v5-2 of the three: on the same jumps as v5-1, it asks Jev first and buys only when Jev gives that side losing steam {{fading}} or less; at most one buy per window, held to the close. Compared with v5-1, it shows whether Jev's check helps.
armIntro.TIMER_JEV: Arm v5-3 of the three: asks Jev every 30 seconds from 60 seconds after the open. When flat, it buys the side ahead if its ask is {{askMin}}¢–{{askMax}}¢ and Jev gives {{against}} or more that BTC's latest step went against that side, in other words it buys the strong side on a pullback; when holding, it sells everything once Jev gives the side it holds a win {{sellWin}} or less. At most one bet at a time, and it can buy again after selling.

jev.armsSub: click a row to open that run
jev.archivedBanner: Viewing archived run {{n}}: it no longer bets, and its bets, decisions and scores stay as they ended.
jev.pnlLabel: PnL this run · settled bets, after fees
jev.scoreDetailsSub: How accurate is Jev's win chance? · {{n}} samples
jev.scoreDetailsSubDecisions: How often it traded, what it paid in fees, what holding would have done
jev.decisionStatsExplain: A look at Jev's trading itself. More trades mean more fees; "If all held" treats every settled buy as never sold and held to the close (buy fees still deducted). Compared with the actual PnL, it shows whether selling helped or hurt.
jev.brierExplain: At every checkpoint the three chances of UP are checked against the result: UP counts as 1, DOWN as 0, and we average (chance − result)². 0 is perfect; 0.25 is what always guessing 50% gets.
jev.brierHow: Watch Jev: lower than Market means Jev reads the window better than the market; lower than Math means it beats the formula that only looks at the gap and the time left. The lowest in each row is orange.
jev.calibration: Calibration: does 70% come true 70% of the time?
jev.calibrationExplain: Jev's chances are split into five bands, and each band shows how often BTC actually finished UP. In the 60%–80% band, roughly seven in ten should have gone UP. The bar is the actual share, the tick is the band's average forecast; the closer the bar's end is to the tick, the better.
jev.guideAction: The first line is what actually happened this time (Buy UP / Buy DOWN / Sell / Hold / Stay out), how much was staked, the time, how many seconds after the open, and a tag for what woke it: always Jump for v5-1 and v5-2, always Timer for v5-3.
jev.guideDecides: The second line is what Jev read from the market: which side this look is about (the side whose price just jumped up on a jump wake; on a timer wake, the side ahead when flat or the side held when holding), Jev's chance that it wins, and what kind of move Jev thinks BTC is in. Jev doesn't make the call; code buys and sells by this arm's rules, and v5-1 only records Jev's answers.
jev.guideUpChance: The "Chance of UP" numbers estimate the same thing — will this window finish above the target price — in different ways:
jev.guideModel: From how far BTC is above the target, how many seconds are left, and how much BTC has been moving lately. Jev doesn't see this number, only a line like "UP ahead by about one normal move"; v5-3 also uses it to pick the side ahead when flat.
jev.guideJev: Jev's estimate: when looking at UP, its chance that UP wins; when looking at DOWN, 1 minus its chance that DOWN wins. In old runs, R1 used the math chance adjusted by Jev's read of the move, R2 and R3 also asked "will this settle UP?" and "will this settle DOWN?" and averaged them, and R5 has no such column.
jev.guideMkt: Derived from the UP and DOWN prices in the order book. With UP around 67¢ and DOWN around 35¢, the market thinks about 66% UP.
jev.guideFold: Rows where a condition failed, routine holds, and rows after this window's buy are folded; use "Show all" on the right of each window. Click any row to see Jev's answer to every question, the book at the time, and UP's mid price 15s and 45s later.
jev.guideLegacy: Runs without an arm name are earlier rules and are shown as they were: in R1 Jev picked the trade itself and judged whether the move still had legs; in R2 Jev only gave a win chance and code bet by comparing it with the asks; in R3 and R4 (v3-2) Jev was asked buy-or-not when flat and hold-or-sell when holding, what it saw included the math estimate and "X¢ cheaper than the estimate", and it was also asked who wins, for scoring only; in R5 (v4) Jev picked one of Buy UP / Buy DOWN / Pass each time and code followed a pick of 50% or more: when flat it bought the side picked; when holding, picking the other side sold everything, picking the side held added a bet (up to $10 on that side per window), and Pass kept holding. In old runs the second line is Jev's pick and confidence, and the "By the math" number after it is for you only: on a buy, how much more each share of that side is worth than it costs (estimated win chance − ask − fee); on hold or sell rows, how much more selling then got per share than the estimate.
jev.guideQuestionsTitle: What Jev is asked each time
jev.guideQuestions: Jev is asked once per wake, and every arm involved in that wake records the same answers. What Jev sees: the rule, the time left, how far BTC is above or below the target, and who is ahead; since the open, in steps of 30 seconds, how BTC moved in each step, whether takers on Binance were mostly buying or selling, and both sides' prices when the step ended; on a jump wake it also says how both prices just jumped. Only facts, never should-buy conclusions. "This side" in the questions is the side this look is about, and Jev gives a probability for each.
jev.qWinDesc: Whether this side wins the window in the end. v5-3 uses it while holding and sells at {{sellWin}} or less; the others only record it.
jev.qPatternTitle: What kind of move is it?
jev.qPatternDesc: How BTC is moving right now. One-way: the price keeps pushing one way with little bounce, and trading pushes the same way. Choppy: the price swings around a level, and moves away get pulled back. No pattern: nothing clear, or barely moving. Recorded only.
jev.qFadingDesc: Earlier steps moved clearly this side's way, but the latest step barely moved or went the other way. v5-2 uses it and doesn't buy above {{fading}}; the others only record it.
jev.qFlowTitle: Is trading pushing this side's way?
jev.qFlowDesc: Whether takers on Binance in the latest step push this side's way: mostly buying for UP, mostly selling for DOWN. Recorded only.
jev.qDipTitle: Did it slip and then pull ahead again?
jev.qDipDesc: Whether BTC moved against this side in an earlier step and back its way in a later one. Recorded only.
jev.qAgainstTitle: Did the latest step go against this side?
jev.qAgainstDesc: Whether BTC's latest step went against this side: a fall when looking at UP, a rise when looking at DOWN; barely moving doesn't count. v5-3 uses it when flat and buys only at {{against}} or more; the others only record it.
jev.guideArms: The three arms watch the same market, each with its own account and run number and its own books; ${{stake}} a bet.

guideArm.JUMP_CODE: Buys the side that rose as soon as a qualifying jump comes, ignoring Jev's answers, and buys even when Jev errors. At most one buy per window, held to the close.
guideArm.JUMP_JEV: On the same jumps, buys only when Jev gives that side losing steam {{fading}} or less. At most one buy per window, held to the close.
guideArm.TIMER_JEV: Wakes at 60, 90 … 270 seconds after the open. When flat it looks at the side ahead and buys if its ask is {{askMin}}¢–{{askMax}}¢ and Jev gives {{against}} or more that BTC's latest step went against it. When holding it looks at the side held and sells everything at the bid once Jev gives it a win {{sellWin}} or less; otherwise it holds. At most one bet at a time, no adding, and it can buy again after selling.

jev.guideJumpDef: A qualifying jump: from 30 to 270 seconds after the open, code checks every second whether UP or DOWN rose {{jump}}¢ or more within 3 seconds from a starting price of {{from}}¢–{{to}}¢. A timer wake right after a jump wake is skipped.
jev.guideCommon: Jev is asked once per wake, and each arm involved writes its own row. Code also blocks mechanical problems: Jev isn't asked when the book or Chainlink has gone stale, and nothing is bought or sold when nobody is selling or bidding on that side or the wallet can't afford a bet. An arm whose wallet can't afford a bet and has no bets waiting to settle stops on its own; the master switch turns off only when all three have stopped.
jev.guideFill: Fills have a delay like a real order: {{delay}}s after deciding, code checks the book once more and every arm involved fills at that book; a buy goes through if the ask is no more than {{tol}}¢ higher, a sell if the bid is no more than {{tol}}¢ lower, otherwise the trade is missed.
jev.q1Title: Does the move still have legs?
